thread:
mira: Heads-up — running into stale API key when we hot-reload the FastAPI dev server. I change REDWOOD_API_KEY in the shell, UVicorn reloads, but async Client still sends old key.

jon: Can you paste the minimal repro? is the client created at import time?

mira: Yep, simplified repro below:

mira: ```python
# app.py (import-time client)
from redwood import Client
client = Client()  # relies on env var REDWOOD_API_KEY

# request handler
async def ping():
    await client.generate("hi")
```

mira: Workflow: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=keyA -> uvicorn --reload app:app -> hit endpoint (works) -> export REDWOOD_API_KEY=keyB -> uvicorn triggers reload -> hit endpoint -> still uses keyA.

sam: That matches fork/reload behavior — when uvicorn reloads it spawns new process but module-level objects may be reimported in a way that keeps previous cached credential provider around for async runtime. Also if you use a long-lived connection pool it can keep auth headers around.

jon: Does Client() accept api_key explicitly? passing it at instantiation should avoid this.

mira: It does, but our codebase creates the client in dozens of modules and a ton of tests rely on env lookup. Changing everywhere is painful.

sam: Short-term workaround: lazily instantiate per-request or add a small wrapper that reads os.environ each call. e.g.

sam: ```python
# lazy wrapper
from redwood import Client
import os
_client = None
def get_client():
    global _client
    key = os.environ.get("REDWOOD_API_KEY")
    if _client is None or _client._api_key != key:
        _client = Client(api_key=key)
    return _client
```

jon: We should fix SDK: two ideas — (1) make the default credential provider read env on each new request when client created with no explicit api_key, or (2) expose an async refresh() that rebinds credentials for long-lived clients. Thoughts?

mira: (2) sounds safer for backwards compat; (1) could surprise folks but is more convenient.

sam: Another angle: document that clients created at import time should pass api_key or use a factory. But yes, an explicit async .refresh_credentials() would be handy for services that reload env.

jon: I'll open a draft PR that: a) adds Client.refresh_credentials()/refresh() coroutine, b) changes the default provider order so explicit api_key > env var > credential chain (no behavior change) but ensures refresh updates cached headers. Also add tests for uvicorn --reload repro.

devex-bot: Related issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/412 (auth: long-lived client env rotation) — please reference when opening PR. :link:

mira: One more gotcha — in our setup we use gunicorn with uvicorn workers in dev; workers fork and inherit file descriptors. If the client keeps connection pools, those sockets can be reused with stale token. So refresh needs to rebuild connector/pool too.

jon: Good call — PR will include pool reinit in refresh. I'll add a warning in the changelog about pool rebuild cost.

ops-bot: FYI: changing default auth semantics could affect enterprise customers using credential rotation. Recommend a feature-flagged rollout and an opt-in config in Dedicated/Private control planes.

mira: Thanks all — i'll open an issue with the uvicorn repro and link our internal service logs. happy to test the PR when it's ready. :+1:

jon: assigning to @sam to shepherd the PR and to @mira for validation steps.
